overviewHtml:
Over-provisioned VMs waste money and under-provisioned ones hurt performance, yet resizing needs an approval step.

What you get

  • A DQL check for Azure hosts with CPU usage above 90% or below 15%
  • A Jira ticket that lists the hosts, plus a Slack notification
  • A second workflow that reacts to the approval event sent back from Jira
  • Resizing through the Azure Compute API, then closing the ticket
prereqsHtml:
• Dynatrace SaaS with Workflows, and Azure VMs monitored by OneAgent. The hosts need Azure subscription and resource group metadata.
  • Jira for Workflows and Slack for Workflows connections
  • An Azure app registration (service principal) with permission to resize the VMs
  • login.microsoftonline.com and management.azure.com in the allowed outbound connections
  • A Jira automation that sends an event to Dynatrace when the ticket is approved
setupHtml:
1. Import both JSON files in Workflows (upload) or with the Automation API.
  2. In each Jira and Slack task, select your connections. The connection IDs were removed from the export.
  3. In Jira, create the approval automation. When an issue moves from Open to Pending, approve it (or let a team approve it), then send a web request to https://.apps.dynatrace.com/api/v2/events/ingest with a CUSTOM_INFO event. That event carries the issue key, URL, ID and description, as shown in the Configuration as Code README.
  4. Set the event trigger of Host Resize - Event Triggered to match that event.
getStartedHtml:
You need Dynatrace Workflows, OneAgent on Azure VMs, Jira and Slack connections and an Azure service principal.

  1. Import both workflows and select your connections
  2. Create the Jira approval automation
  3. Match the event trigger to that automation
